explanation: Track the farthest reachable index. Every position up to that boundary is reachable, so processing it can extend the boundary. A gap before the final position proves failure.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: After processing a reachable index, farthest is the greatest index reachable using processed positions. Every position up to that bound is reachable because a jump permits every distance up to its maximum. If the next index exceeds the bound, no later position can be reached to extend it.
walkthrough: For [2,0,1,0], index 0 reaches through index 2. Index 1 adds no reach, but reachable index 2 extends the bound to 3, the last position. Return true.
edgeCases: A single position is already the end.
A zero before an unreachable suffix can block all progress.
Reach calculations use long so a large allowed offset does not overflow.
